title: Model capability manifest + version-pinning API: schema additions and publish flow
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary:
We need to extend the public model/catalog API and the internal publishing path so that every model in the catalog exposes a stable, machine-readable "manifest" (capabilities + profiles) and supports explicit version pinning semantics. The goal is to let clients discover exact runtime limits and feature flags (context window, max_tokens, streaming support, function calling, quantized variants, kernel compatibility, latency/throughput profiles) and to allow safe pinning to variants of a model when customers request a deterministic serving contract.

Background / motivation:
- Customers request the ability to pin to a model version/variant for repeatable behavior and audits.
- Console and autoscaler need per-variant performance profiles to make routing and capacity decisions (latency p50/p95, tokens/sec, memory estimate).
- Current /models list is opaque: fields are inconsistent and don't include performance characteristics or explicit version IDs for deployment artifacts.

High-level deliverables:
1) API schema additions to GET /models and GET /models/:id to include a top-level "manifest" object describing capabilities and a list of "profiles" with metric summaries.
2) Control-plane publishing flow (internal CLI + service) to register a model artifact + profile document as an immutable version (semantic variant id).
3) Version pinning semantics exposed via the runtime API (allow clients to specify pin_by: "variant" or "major", and server-side validation/compatibility checks).
4) Backwards-compatible rollout strategy and deprecation plan for the old opaque fields.

Note: the description below includes a suggested schema example and operational notes — this ticket covers the API/schema and publishing flow; storage/migration and console UX tickets will follow or be linked.
acceptance_criteria: GET /models returns a new 'manifest' field for all newly published models and existing models after migration; unknown clients must be ignored gracefully
Manifest includes 'capabilities' and 'profiles' arrays with documented keys (context_window, max_tokens, streaming, function_calling, deterministic, embeddings_supported, quantized_variants)
Control-plane publish endpoint accepts a model artifact + profile JSON and writes an immutable variant_id (format: <model>-vYYYYMMDD-hex4)
Runtime accepts requests with 'version_pin' parameter and routes to the pinned variant when capacity exists, otherwise follows configured fallback policies
Automated tests that verify schema validation, storage immutability, and runtime routing to pinned variants
Security review completed and schema does not expose sensitive internal metrics (only aggregated performance summaries)
Documentation (OpenAPI spec + SDK changelog) updated and a migration note published for existing customers
Rollback path documented and smoke test runbook created for the first two customer rollouts
implementation_notes: API: add 'manifest' (stringified JSON schema example in docs) to GET /models and GET /models/:id responses; add POST /models/:id/publish to create a variant
DB: new 'model_variants' table with columns: variant_id (pk), model_id, artifact_ref, manifest_blob, published_by, published_at; migration script must backfill minimal manifest for existing models
Control plane: new publishing service that validates manifest against JSON schema and generates variant_id; store manifest immutably
Runtime: support 'version_pin' header and behavior: if 'variant' -> exact variant_id; if 'major' -> allow compatible minor updates per compatibility label in manifest
Compatibility rules: manifest must include 'compatibility_hash' computed at build time; runtime verifies hash when routing across clusters
Telemetry: capture routing decisions, pin failures, and fallback events as events with tag 'variant_pin' for investigation
Quota/limits: manifest must include max_concurrent_requests and max_batch_size so autoscaler can reserve capacity
migration_plan: Phase 1 (read-only): publish manifest field on GET endpoints for newly onboarded models and for any variant published after 2026-03-15. Phase 2 (backfill): run a backfill to synthesize best-effort manifests for existing entries (marked 'inferred') and surface a 'manifest_source' flag. Phase 3 (publish APIs): enable POST /models/:id/publish and start creating immutable variants for model onboarding pipeline. Phase 4 (pinning): runtime accepts 'version_pin' and route policies; begin opt-in with 3 pilot customers. Phase 5 (enforce): after pilot validation, flip default behavior for reserved/dedicated customers and document deprecation of old opaque fields (90-day notice).
notes: Design sync held 2026-02-25: agreed on read-first rollout to avoid breaking SDKs
Security: manifest must not include raw memory addresses or internal node IDs (we will aggregate to 'memory_estimate_mb')
Naming: use 'variant_id' instead of 'version' to avoid confusion with package versions
